PHARMACEUTICAL CHEMISTRY, PH.D.
Graduate Coordinator: Dr. Thomas Coombs
The Pharmaceutical Chemistry Ph.D. ensures that UNCW students are prepared for a flexible career in pharmaceutical chemistry. The Chemistry & Biochemistry faculty enable this goal by offering a broad range of pharmaceutical chemistry courses and research foci, from traditional and non-traditional natural products drug discovery and medicinal chemistry to formulation of therapeutic antibodies. In addition to employment opportunities in the pharmaceutical industry, graduates of this program will be ideally positioned to work in the rapidly expanding contract research (CRO) and biotechnology sectors, pursue academic careers, or establish innovative start-up companies. Bolstered by a generous endowment from Dr. Yousry and Linda Sayed, former UNCW faculty members and founders of Quality Chemistry Laboratories, this program is one of the most rapidly growing initiatives at UNCW.
Admission Requirements
Students can enter the Ph.D. in Pharmaceutical Chemistry program in the following three ways:
1. Students with a M.S in Chemistry or other STEM-related discipline entering directly into the Ph.D. program, or
2. Students with a B.S. (based on a 4-year program) in Chemistry or other STEM-related discipline entering the MS in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and transitioning into the Ph.D. program, or
3. Students with a B.S. in Chemistry or other STEM-related discipline entering directly into the Ph.D. program.
Minimum requirements for students in categories 1 and 2
a. An overall grade point average of at least 3.0 out of 4.0 for the most recent degree earned.
b. For applicants whose native language is not English: Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) with a score of at least 550 on the paper test or 79 on the online test, or International English Language Testing System (IELTS) with a score of 6.5 or 7.0.
Minimum requirements for students in category 3
a. An overall grade point average of at least 3.5 out of 4.0.
b. For applicants whose native language is not English: Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) with a score of at least 550 on the paper test or 79 on the online test, or International English Language Testing System (IELTS) with a score of 6.5 or 7.0.
c. Evidence of independent research.
Candidates admitted to our master’s program can apply for the Ph.D. program after 2 years with approval of the graduate committee and the thesis advisor.
Documents to be submitted for admission
UNC Wilmington application for graduate admission
Transcripts of all college work (undergraduate and graduate)
Curriculum vita
Official score on the TOEFL (if applicable).
A minimum of three letters of recommendations from individuals who are knowledgeable of the student’s academic acumen and ability to complete the Ph.D. degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry
A personal statement describing educational, professional and research experiences, career goals and reasons for pursuing the Ph.D. degree
Abstract from the student’s master’s thesis research (optional)
Copies of publications (optional)
Degree Requirements
The Pharmaceutical Chemistry Ph.D. requires a total of 60 credits post-baccalaureate including 40 credits post-masters.
The 60 credits (post-M.S.) will come from coursework, research, and dissertation at the doctoral level. We divide those credits into three categories: core Chemistry courses (15 credits), electives (9 credits), and directed individual study and dissertation (36 credits).
Required Core Courses (15 hours)
CHM 501 - Introduction to Chemical Research Credit Hours: 2
CHM 595 - Graduate Seminar Credit Hours: 1 to 3
CHM 505 - Pharmaceutical Chemistry I: Introduction to Drug Discovery Credit Hours: 3
CHM 506 - Pharmaceutical Chemistry II: Pharmaceutical Analysis Credit Hours: 3
And at least two of the following courses:
CHM 516 - Advanced Organic Chemistry Credit Hours: 3
CHM 536 - Advanced Analytical Chemistry Credit Hours: 3
CHM 568 - Advanced Biochemistry Credit Hours: 3
Electives (9 hours)
Three additional 500- or 600-level courses from the following list (9 credits):
CHM 507 - Pharmacokinetics Credit Hours: 3
CHM 508 - Formulation Development of Biologics Credit Hours: 3
CHM 512 - Structure Elucidation Credit Hours: 3
CHM 516 - Advanced Organic Chemistry Credit Hours: 3
CHM 517 - Medicinal Chemistry Credit Hours: 3
CHM 518 - Pharmaceutical Process Chemistry Credit Hours: 3
CHM 521 - Advanced Physical Chemistry Credit Hours: 3
CHM 525 - Molecular Modeling Credit Hours: 3
CHM 536 - Advanced Analytical Chemistry Credit Hours: 3
CHM 546 - Advanced Inorganic Chemistry Credit Hours: 3
CHM 562 - Cell Signaling Credit Hours: 3
CHM 568 - Advanced Biochemistry Credit Hours: 3
BIO 515 - Introductory Biostatistics Credit Hours: 3
CLR 545 - Biopharmaceutical Technology Management Credit Hours: 3
ENG 575 - Professional Science Writing Credit Hours: 3
PAR 515 - Ethical Issues in Research Credit Hours: 1 To 3
Directed Individual Study and Dissertation (36 hours)
36 credit hours are required from the following list:
CHM 691 - Directed Individual Study Credit Hours: 1 To 9
CHM 692 - Dissertation Proposal Credit Hours: 3
CHM 698 - Dissertation Research Credit Hours: 1 to 12
CHM 699 - Dissertation Credit Hours: 1 to 12
Total Credit Hours: 60
